title: Audit logging: rollout policy change event types + before/after diff payloads
author: Kevin Osei
body:
Summary: This PR adds first-class audit log event types for Hosted rollout policy changes and standardizes the payload to include a redacted before/after diff. This is part of canary rollouts GA readiness and unblocks compliance requests for an immutable trail of who changed rollout routing and when.

What’s included (high level): 1) New audit event types: rollout_policy.created, rollout_policy.updated, rollout_policy.paused, rollout_policy.rolled_back. 2) Payload shape standardized across these events with common fields (actor, org, project, route, rollout_id, policy_version, request_id, source) + change payload fields (before_redacted, after_redacted, diff). 3) A deterministic diff generator (JSON Patch-like) to avoid emitting full policy objects when large; diff is computed after canonicalization (sorted keys, stable array ordering where applicable) so exports don’t churn. 4) Redaction rules for sensitive fields (no prompts, no customer headers, no auth tokens); guardrail thresholds and weights are allowed. 5) Export compatibility: fields are flat-ish and stable so they can be shipped to SIEM without downstream schema drift.

Motivation / context: Customers in regulated environments asked for an audit trail of rollout changes (who created/updated/paused/rolled back a rollout, and what changed). Today we emit generic “policy updated” events with minimal context, and support has to reconstruct diffs from DB history. For GA, we need explicit event types and structured before/after metadata. Related: ENG-8426, rollout change endpoints in PR #18435, policy schema v2 in PR #18421.

Implementation notes: - Audit events are emitted in the control-plane service at the point where the rollout policy transaction commits (post-validation, post-normalization). - The “before” snapshot is read inside the same transaction (SELECT … FOR UPDATE) to ensure the before/after pair is consistent. - For update/pause/rollback, the event includes both the redacted objects and a compact diff. For create, before is null and diff is omitted. - Diff generation: canonicalize -> compute per-field changes; arrays are treated as replace operations (we avoid element-level diffs to reduce complexity and prevent noisy diffs when step schedules reorder). - Size limiting: if after_redacted exceeds 48KB, we omit before_redacted/after_redacted and emit only diff + a “payload_truncated=true” marker (still included in export). - Actor attribution: supports both end-user actions (Console/API) and service actors; includes actor_type=user|service and actor_id plus display fields if available.

Security / privacy: - Explicit allowlist for policy fields that may be emitted (weights, variant identifiers, guardrails config, rollout state, schedule metadata). - Explicit denylist for request headers, customer-provided metadata, and any freeform string fields not part of the allowlist. - No prompt text, no model outputs, no customer IP. - Diff is computed after redaction.

Changed areas: - control-plane/audit: Adds rollout policy event constants + schema. - control-plane/rollouts: Emits events for create/update/pause/rollback paths. - common/audit: Adds redaction + canonicalization helpers and unit tests. - docs (internal): Updates audit event catalog with the new types and examples.

Tests: - Unit tests for redaction allowlist/denylist behavior and for diff stability across key ordering. - Integration tests for each endpoint to ensure the expected event type and required fields are emitted.

Release note (internal): Audit logs now include explicit Hosted rollout change events with structured diffs for create/update/pause/rollback. No customer-facing API changes.

Commits: 1) audit: add rollout_policy.* event types + schema 2) rollouts: emit audit events on create/update 3) rollouts: emit audit events on pause/rollback 4) audit: add redaction + canonicalization helpers 5) tests: integration coverage for event payloads

Files changed (high level): - services/control-plane/src/audit/events.ts - services/control-plane/src/audit/redaction.ts - services/control-plane/src/audit/diff.ts - services/control-plane/src/rollouts/rollout_service.ts - services/control-plane/src/rollouts/rollout_handlers.ts - services/control-plane/test/audit/rollout_policy_events.test.ts - services/control-plane/test/integration/rollouts_audit_events.test.ts - docs/internal/security/audit-event-catalog.md

Example payload (illustrative, not exact): Event type: rollout_policy.updated. Includes org_id, project_id, route_id, rollout_id, actor, occurred_at, before_redacted, after_redacted, and diff entries like: replace /traffic_split/weights/candidate from 10 to 25, replace /guardrails/error_rate_threshold from 0.02 to 0.01.

Review conversation (highlights): - Marcus Lin: “We should not emit full before/after objects by default; SIEM pipelines will choke on large payloads. Can we make diff the primary payload and gate full objects behind size limits?” - Kevin Osei (author): “Updated. Added 48KB cap and default to include both before/after only if under cap; otherwise diff-only with payload_truncated=true. Also switched diff computation to run after redaction.” - Chloe Martin: “Idempotency: can we end up double-emitting events on retry? We need a stable request_id and dedupe semantics.” - Kevin Osei: “Good catch. Wired through x-request-id from the handler context and included it in the audit payload. Also added an event_id generated deterministically from (event_type, rollout_id, policy_version, request_id) so downstream can dedupe.” - Jordan Lee: “For rollback, the ‘before’ should be the currently-effective policy, and ‘after’ is the previous version we’re restoring. Ensure policy_version increments monotonically.” - Kevin Osei: “Adjusted rollback path to record before=effective@N, after=restored@N+1. Added test asserting monotonic version increments.” - Marcus Lin: “Please confirm we’re not leaking model prompt templates or customer metadata via the policy object.” - Kevin Osei: “Confirmed. Policy schema doesn’t include prompts; added denylist for any freeform ‘metadata’ keys and a test to enforce we drop unknown keys.

CI: - 2024-10-04: build_and_test failed (eslint: unused import in diff.ts) -> fixed in commit 3c8f9e1 - 2024-10-07: integration tests flaky due to clock precision in occurred_at assertions -> updated tests to assert RFC3339 parseability and presence, not exact equality - 2024-10-08: all checks passing

Merge: Squash merged into main.

Follow-ups (not blocking): - Add dashboard/export docs snippet for customers on Enterprise compliance package (tracked in ENG-8430 / Security enablement). - Consider adding “policy_hash” to payload for quick equality checks (would help support triage; optional).
